rewrite.summary: UH Manoa libraries research guide on Pacific gender identities (maintained; last updated 2026-07-23). Contains substantive American Samoa content: the Society of Fa'afafine in American Samoa (SOFIAS) was formed in 2010 by merging the American Samoa Island Queens Association and the American 7s Association, explicitly re-anchored to cultural pride - 'we are fa'afafine Samoa'. It defines fa'afafine as born male but embodying both male and female traits, 'a recognized and integral part of traditional Samoan culture', and frames colonial suppression followed by contemporary reclaiming of Pacific gender identities.

Out Traveler 'Ask the Expert' column (Ed Salvato, 2009-07-01) answering a honeymoon question about American Samoa: the two Samoan nations share the fa'amatai chiefly system; ASM's ~57,000 residents across seven islands/atolls; 'Samoan culture tends toward traditionalism, and reserved behavior by people of all orientations is expected', yet 'unlike the homophobia rampant in Fiji, homosexuality is a widely accepted part of Samoan culture', with Western gay men reportedly courted by fa'afafine transgender locals and by officially straight men; local artist Dan Taulapapa McMullin calls the Samoan islands 'the homeland of fa'afafine culture'; ASM hotels skew business-travel (Tradewinds, Pago Pago).

The Independent, 2015-07-10: American Samoa was the only US territory unsure whether Obergefell applied - AG Talauega Eleasalo Ale: 'We're still reviewing the decision to determine its applicability to American Samoa... I don't know. We're reviewing the law', while Puerto Rico, USVI, Guam and CNMI moved to apply it. ~50,000 residents, conservative Christian, motto 'Samoa, Muia God e Muamua'. Fa'afafine tradition noted; leading figure Princess Auvaa says many fa'afafine don't push gay marriage out of respect for culture/religion, yet would herself be first to apply for a licence. No same-sex marriage licence applications had been made; territorial-law experts (Villazor, Keitner) said recognition required voluntary adoption or litigation, warning the review had a chilling effect.

add.title: American Samoa Senate rejects bill outlawing same sex marriages (RNZ Pacific)
add.summary: American Samoa's Fono Senate voted down a bill that would have outlawed same-sex marriage in March 2003, after the House judiciary committee recommended the bill be killed. The bill was introduced by Representative Sua Carl Schuster, who wanted to preempt the kind of marriage lawsuits then unfolding in US states. At the committee hearing, fa'afafine resident Tifanny Poutasi testified that Samoan fa'afafine 'don't believe in marriages with other men', describing them as men expressing femininity through dress and speech who do not seek same-sex marriage, citing Christian upbringing. For this record: documents that the territory deliberately declined a formal marriage ban pre-Obergefell, and gives contemporaneous local fa'afafine voices on the question.

add.title: American Samoa judge objects to same sex marriage (RNZ Pacific)
add.summary: In January 2016 the American Samoa Senate unanimously confirmed former territory Attorney General Fiti Alexander Sunia as District Court judge, filling the seat left by Judge John Ward II's retirement. At his confirmation hearing Senator Tauolo Manaia Fruean, a retired associate judge of the High Court of American Samoa, asked whether Sunia had read Obergefell; Sunia replied he had not read the US Supreme Court decision and that the district court 'doesn't deal with this ruling', and said he would not perform weddings for same-sex couples unless local laws are changed. For this record: direct evidence that eighteen months after Obergefell the territory's judiciary was operating on the premise it did not automatically apply, with named actors and dates.

add.title: The Ambiguity that Isn't: Why Same-Sex Marriage Is Legal in American Samoa (Harootunian & Lawrence, American University JGSPL vol 33 iss 2 (2026) pp 163-207)
add.summary: 2026 law review article by two attorneys practicing in American Samoa (American Samoa Legal Aid, with Freedom From Religion Foundation) concluding that Obergefell DOES apply in the territory despite local officials' statements, and that American Samoa would have to issue a marriage certificate to any same-sex couple that applied. It records that to date no same-sex couple has applied for a marriage license in the territory, and lays out the litigation roadmap: the High Court of American Samoa first (defendant the Territorial Registrar), then the US Department of the Interior. For this record: the freshest dated authority on the exact open question (is the 2015 ruling operative in ASM?), and it separates the law from the practical reality (no licenses sought/issued).

add.title: Survey conducted on-island focuses on local same sex marriage ban (Samoa News, Asi Andrew Fa'asau, Pago Pago)
add.summary: Samoa News reported in July 2024 an on-island survey by Dr Daniel Hall, a constitutional and comparative law professor at Miami University, testing whether American Samoa's same-sex marriage ban would survive a challenge under the 14th Amendment. The survey also probes cultural dimensions bearing on the question (collectivistic vs individualistic orientation; linear vs polychronic time). For this record: as of mid-2024, nine years after Obergefell and more than a year after the Respect for Marriage Act obliged recognition of outside marriages (Dec 13 2022), the local ban is treated on-island as operative and its constitutional durability as an open question.
